summary: @servicetitan/table preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`, which auto-executes on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods the binary 0755, and then invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'], {stdio:'inherit'})`. The bundled sibling `math_init.js` is a ~727KB Bun-compiled bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) that is heavily obfuscated with obfuscator.io fingerprints: a string-array rotation function (`WV8StW`), a large numeric/opcode array (`n7gIxM`), and a custom-alphabet character decoder (`hc1jfK9`). The file name and payload have no relationship to the package's stated purpose as a React data-table component library. Selecting an alternate JavaScript runtime (Bun) specifically to execute an obfuscated sibling on install is an evasion pattern that prevents Node-based scanners and inspection tooling from analyzing the code that actually runs on the installer's machine. Result: arbitrary code execution on every installer host at install time, under obfuscation, via a runtime fetched over the network.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
